chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in one of his military expeditions when they complained to him about the fleas that they were hurting them. So he said: 'When one of you takes his bed, let him say:'

O the black leaper who does not care about a lock nor a door! I have sworn an oath upon you by the Mother of the Book that you shall not hurt me or my companions until the night departs and the morning comes with whatever it brings, and the morning that we know, until the morning returns, whenever it returns.

key_terms.أُمِّ الْكِتَابِ: The Mother of the Book (referring to Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for protection from fleas before sleeping in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the practical application of reciting Al-Fatiha as a potent means of protection (ruqyah) against specific nuisances, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Quran's inherent power. The address to the flea as 'the black leaper' (al-aswad al-waththab) personifies the creature, while invoking the 'Mother of the Book' underscores the belief that the Quran itself serves as a shield against harm. This practice illustrates the integration of spiritual reliance with daily life, a key theme in Twelver Shi'ite devotional traditions.
